related_work_items.paper_title: Robust self-paced hashing for cross-modal retrieval with noisy labels

evidence.evidence_text: RSHNL [31] designs a Robust Self-paced Hashing mechanism that mitigates the misleading effects of noisy labels on the model by simulating the human cognitive process.

RSHNL [31] proposes a robust self-paced hashing mechanism that emulates human cognition, thereby reducing the negative impact of noisy labels and improving model performance. However, in real-world applications, multimodal annotations often contain "redundant annotations".

In this work, we compare our NACD against 11 state-of-the-art CMH methods, including five unsupervised methods: DJSRH [18], DGCPN [20], PIP [49], CIRH [21], and UCCH [22]; and six supervised methods: CMMQ [50], MIAN [27], LtCMH [28], DHRL [29], NRCH [30], and RSHNL [31].

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: RSHNL is a strong noisy-label CMH baseline, but the paper argues it still assumes label corruption by replacement rather than redundant candidate label sets.

evidence.evidence_text: Within a probabilistic modality alignment framework, MIAN [27] investigates the preservation of asymmetric similarities both within and between modalities, thereby fully utilizing multi-level semantic information throughout the entire database.

In this work, we compare our NACD against 11 state-of-the-art CMH methods, including five unsupervised methods: DJSRH [18], DGCPN [20], PIP [49], CIRH [21], and UCCH [22]; and six supervised methods: CMMQ [50], MIAN [27], LtCMH [28], DHRL [29], NRCH [30], and RSHNL [31].

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: MIAN represents supervised CMH methods that leverage clean label information effectively but are not designed for redundant candidate-label supervision.

related_work_items.paper_title: Global-local label correlation for partial multi-label learning

evidence.evidence_text: Although partial multi-label learning (PML) [32][33][34][35] provides a potential solution for redundant annotations, most PML methods assume a shared feature space and overlook cross-modal semantic divergence.
The sparsity regularization-based approaches [32,33,40] impose sparsity on the candidate label set, effectively suppressing noisy labels and facilitating disambiguation.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: This PML work is part of the paper's nearest label-disambiguation lineage, but the paper argues that PML methods do not address cross-modal divergence and robust pair construction.

evidence.evidence_text: Although partial multi-label learning (PML) [32][33][34][35] provides a potential solution for redundant annotations, most PML methods assume a shared feature space and overlook cross-modal semantic divergence.
Smoothness assumption-based approaches [35,37,38] are based on the assumption that neighboring samples in the feature space are more likely to have similar labels.

related_work_items.gap_relevance_note: This neighborhood-based PML paper is especially close to NACD's confidence reconstruction intuition, while NACD adapts the idea to cross-modal neighbors and hashing.
